newsitem.title: USA: US money managers more bullish Nov 19 wk -- survey.
newsitem.headline: US money managers more bullish Nov 19 wk -- survey.

text.p: Money managers continued to grow more bullish on U.S. debt markets in the past week, extending their durations to higher levels, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"The gradual process of duration extension continued this past week," the report said."
"As a result of this week's activity, the average duration ratio rose to 101.7 percent, the highest reading since February 1996," the report said.

In the week ended November 19, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading rose to 5.02 from 4.82 the prior week; the asset-weighted number climbed to 4.80 from 4.69 in the week ended November 12, according to the report.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio fell to 6.52 percent from 6.81 percent.
Duration bogey rose modestly to 4.12 on an arithmetic basis and rose to 4.69 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Sixteen percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 28 percent the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was 5.75, down from 6.14 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
